messages:
Noah Reed: Heads-up — Experiments team at BetaCo is hitting intermittent 401/403 on the POC. Root call is /v1/generate. They report some success then 403s and sporadic 429s. Key used: beta_poc_key1.
Sofia Kim: Can you share one failing curl and the raw response?
Noah Reed: Here's what they ran:
```
curl -v POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer beta_poc_key1' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"Forbidden","message":"key org != request org","details":"token_org=org-b42 request_org=org-b99"}
```
Noah Reed: They are not intentionally sending x-redwood-org; suspect our client library adds it in their scaffold. Request id in logs: r-a9b8c7d6.
Devon (Support): Looks like an org-binding mismatch. Could also be a scoped key (e.g., embeddings-only) used for generation. Can you introspect the key from the admin API? `GET /v1/admin/keys/beta_poc_key1`
Noah Reed: Introspect returned (sanitized): `{ "key":"beta_poc_key1","org_id":"org-b42","scopes":["embeddings.write"],"created_by":"sales-demo" }`
Sofia Kim: Yep — key is org-b42 and doesn't have generate scope. Their harness is instantiating cloud-tenant header org-b99 somewhere.
Priya Rao: Quick unblock options: 1) Generate a new key under org-b99 with generate scope. 2) Remove forced org header from their client. 3) Use an account-level key. Which do they prefer?
Noah Reed: BetaCo wants the least friction. I'll spin a new key for org-b99 with `api:generate`. Trying now.
Devon (Support): Also FYI we rolled out stricter org validation on generate endpoints last week — mismatched headers now return 403 instead of falling back. That changed a few POCs.
Noah Reed: New key made: beta_poc_key2 (scopes: api:generate). Initial smoke tests passed but after ~40s the harness saw 429 TooManyRequests with retry_after 8. They run 30 parallel workers in CI.
Sofia Kim: That's likely per-key QPS limits. For POC can open a temporary request to SRE for a short uplift. If sustained, we should propose Dedicated slots (quote required).
Priya Rao: Devon, can we get a temporary uplift for account beta-enterprises-77 for 12 hours? Provide request id and desired QPS.
Devon (Support): Please submit this short request form: https://console.redwood.ai/support/poc-rate-uplift — include account id, request id r-a9b8c7d6, and desired concurrency/qps. I'll attach to the SRE ticket.
Noah Reed: Submitted form with QPS=120 and account beta-enterprises-77.
deploy-bot: SRE ticket created: SRE-7753. Pending review.
Devon (Support): While we wait, recommend BetaCo throttle concurrency to ~8-10 and add exponential backoff on 429s to avoid hitting system limits.
Sofia Kim: Also add in the security answers: hosted keys are rotateable in Console, and private deployments can integrate with customer KMS. They asked specifically if we can rotate keys without downtime — yes for hosted if you prepare a new key and update clients; we have a runbook.
Noah Reed: They also asked for audit logs & rotation cadence for compliance. Can someone drop the runbook and audit link in this thread?
Devon (Support): I'll upload the runbook and a sanitized example audit export to the deal folder. Also, for rotation automation, recommend using key aliases and short TTLs. I'll follow up in the deal.
deploy-bot: Temporary rate uplift granted for 12h on SRE-7753 at 2201112234 (QPS +30%).
Noah Reed: Re-tested after uplift — POC completed full test matrix. Customer wants the uplift invoice and a note on long-term options (Dedicated pricing + entitlements).
Sofia Kim: I'll prepare a draft quote and include Dedicated starter pricing plus an option for reserved throughput for the trial.
Devon (Support): Closing swarm for now — saved runbook and audit sample in the deal folder. Re-open if BetaCo sees regressions. :white_check_mark:
